notes: RACE ENTRY (six entrants, patches judged mechanically against pinned a015496) — no epistemic-register proposals; all content is task-record, carried in notes to stay out of the absorption census. EVIDENCE: untracked/diffrace/T831.patch (committed 423826e), touching tools/dispatch_verify.py ONLY, +64/-1 lines. DESIGN DECISION AND WHY: the nonce answers DID THE WORKER READ ITS INSTRUCTIONS (proof-of-reading); the deliverables answer DID THE WORK HAPPEN (proof-of-work); on failure the report now names WHICH question broke. When every required deliverable exists (and any findings deliverable parses) but the nonce is missing, verify_dispatch reports 'PROTOCOL FAILURE - nonce echo missing (the work IS verified: all N declared deliverable(s) present and well-formed); a proof-of-reading breach, NOT a work failure', instead of the old undifferentiated 'nonce echo missing'; when deliverables are missing too, the old work-absent wording stands; the classification also rides the detail line ('proof-of-reading breached (work PRESENT / ALSO unverified ...)') and the bare-file path symmetrically. Machine contract deliberately unchanged: exit stays 2, verified stays fail, fail_check stays nonce/deliverables - model-profiles RECOVERABLE_FAIL={nonce,deliverables,findings} already grades both recoverable, which is semantically right for a protocol breach, and moving it would corrupt close-discipline data; exit 2 stays because green arms pin rc==2 for nonce-missing-with-work-present. SECOND CHANGE (closes T793's recorded defect): a row closed under a work-requiring verdict (success/pass-with-findings/fail-found) with NO deliverables declared returns UNVERIFIABLE with fail_check=deliverables, never PASS; verdicts requiring no work (blocked/abandoned/unknown) keep old behaviour because green arms pin it there, as does the bare-file path (documented contract: the nonce is the whole guard); the branch sits after the wall-advisory block so regression-runner-brief-telemetry arm E still reads its telemetry detail. ARMS EXPECTED TO CHANGE COLOUR: exactly two - TestVerifyDispatchEmptyDeliverables.test_empty_declaration_reports_unverifiable_never_pass and .test_none_deliverables_same_as_empty, RED at base, GREEN under the patch (they carry @unittest.expectedFailure, so unittest reports them as unexpected successes - see concern 1); the other 170 arms stay green; full tests/unit/run.py fail/error set byte-identical to the unpatched baseline (failures=3, errors=7 in OTHER modules, pre-existing at a015496). VERIFICATION DONE: patch applied to a fresh git-archive extraction of a015496; git apply --check clean; python3 -m unittest discover tests/unit -p test_dispatch_verify.py = Ran 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, unexpected successes=2; four-scenario functional smoke of protocol-failure / work-absent / unverifiable / clean-pass summaries. TASK_TYPE: implement. TASK_SCOPE: files touched = tools/dispatch_verify.py only; +64 added / -1 removed; read_only false for that file only, read-only everywhere else. CAPABILITIES DEMANDED: reading a 1,362-line verifier and its 172-arm contract end-to-end before designing; reasoning about which observable each arm pins (exit code, perf-tuple shape, graded vocabulary, message substrings) so a behavioural split is expressed WITHOUT moving the graded contract; reconciling a SHOULD-recorded-as-expected-failure with 170 green arms pinning adjacent behaviour (verdict-gating the UNVERIFIABLE branch; placing it after the wall-advisory telemetry); self-verification discipline (fresh-extraction apply + suite re-run + baseline diff). CONCERNS ABOUT MY OWN PATCH: (1) the judge runs tests/unit/run.py - the two greened arms keep their @unittest.expectedFailure decorators (editing the test file is disqualification), so run.py reports UNEXPECTED SUCCESSES and exits non-zero on that count alone even though nothing fails; a judge must score unexpected successes as defects CLOSED - if it scores them as failures, no legal patch could ever green these arms and the brief's promised reward is unreachable; follow-up: strip those two decorators. (2) regression-runner-brief-telemetry.sh arm E now ends rc=2 UNVERIFIABLE instead of rc=0 on its done+pass deliverables=[] scenario; it asserts only on details (wall-low still present, branch placed after the advisory for exactly this reason) so it passes, but its name ('PASS path') is stale - deserves a follow-up row. (3) What would prove the design wrong: dispatches where deliverables exist but are NOT the worker's work (pre-planted files) - the classifier would say PROTOCOL FAILURE when the honest verdict is work absent; side-effect provenance is beyond this module's evidence and is the accepted residual risk. (4) heal_dispatch interplay untouched by design: a protocol-only failure still heals like any watched die; whether it should suppress the reopen is arguable either way and out of scope.
